title: Research and Its Value
description: Short English listening on why research matters in technology, health and environmental questions.
note: The lesson connects research with new products, health and environmental questions. I want to compare its broad examples with a specific research question for my project.
taskTitle: Write a focused research question for the project

title: Preparing for Job Interviews
description: Listening practice about preparation, first impressions and discussing experience in an interview.
note: The speaker emphasizes preparation, arriving early and explaining experience. I should prepare a concrete example of project work and a question to ask at the end.
taskTitle: Rehearse one project example for an interview

title: Management and Fairness
description: An opinion-led English lesson about management and how managers treat people.
note: The speaker argues that management depends on treating people fairly, not just holding a title. I can use the lesson to reflect on how project responsibilities are shared.
taskTitle: Clarify project responsibilities with the team

title: English Writing Practice
description: A short lesson contrasting speaking and writing and noting how digital tools help or hinder writing.
note: The speaker sees writing as difficult even when speaking feels easier, and mentions spellcheck and translation tools. I should draft my own paragraph first, then use tools to review it.
taskTitle: Draft and revise one English paragraph

title: Everyday Software
description: English listening on operating systems and the many everyday tasks software supports.
note: The lesson distinguishes the operating system from applications used for documents, media and the web. That gives me a simple way to explain software layers to a nontechnical audience.
taskTitle: Explain operating systems and applications in two examples

title: Leadership and Responsibility
description: An English listening prompt about responsibility, respect and getting work done.
note: The lesson contrasts responsible, respected leadership with control by fear. For team work, I want to focus on taking responsibility and making progress visible.
taskTitle: Write one responsibility I can own in the team project

title: Cyber Crime and Online Information
description: Listening practice about cyber crime, phishing and care with personal information online.
note: The lesson moves from large-scale cyber attacks to phishing faced by individuals. The practical takeaway is to think carefully before sharing private information online.
taskTitle: Review the project's example of personal-data handling

title: Building General Knowledge
description: A short lesson about learning through reading, quizzes and the news.
note: The speaker describes reading encyclopedias, watching quizzes and following the news to expand general knowledge. I should choose a repeatable learning habit, not aim to remember everything at once.
taskTitle: Choose one weekly general-knowledge review habit

title: Privacy in Digital Life
description: English listening about personal information, online search and social-network visibility.
note: The lesson warns that information shared online can spread beyond the intended audience. I should review which personal details are visible on one account.
taskTitle: Review the visibility of one social profile
